content: Sotagliflozin is a dual inhibitor of SGLT1 and SGLT2 that has recently been approved by the FDA. Its primary purpose is to reduce the risk of cardiovascular death, hospitalizations due to heart failure, and urgent visits for heart failure in patients with type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease (CKD), or other cardiovascular risk factors. Unlike other SGLT2 inhibitors, sotagliflozin also inhibits SGLT1, which slows glucose absorption in the intestine. This dual mechanism provides more comprehensive glycemic control and makes it effective for managing both type 1 and type 2 diabetes. In clinical trials, sotagliflozin demonstrated significant cardiovascular benefits. The SCORED trial, which included 10,584 participants, compared sotagliflozin to a placebo. The results showed that sotagliflozin reduced the incidence of heart failure events, with 5.6 events per 100 patient-years in the sotagliflozin group compared to 7.5 events per 100 patient-years in the placebo group. The SOLOIST-WHF trial focused on patients with worsening heart failure. Participants were randomized to receive either sotagliflozin or a placebo. Those treated with sotagliflozin experienced a significantly lower rate of urgent heart failure-related visits. However, sotagliflozin is associated with gastrointestinal side effects, such as diarrhea, which occur more frequently compared to other SGLT2 inhibitors. This is due to its inhibition of SGLT1, which increases sugar levels in the gut and impacts the gastrointestinal system. While sotagliflozin effectively reduces cardiovascular morbidity, it has not been shown to significantly reduce all-cause mortality.
